legend: Dreamoon likes sequences very much. So he created a problem about the sequence that you can't find in OEIS:
You are given two integers d,m%%ZSMJ0%%, find the number of arrays a%%ZSMJ1%%, satisfying the following constraints:
The length of a%%ZSMJ2%% is n%%ZSMJ3%%, n≥1%%ZSMJ4%%

Define an array b%%ZSMJ6%% of length n%%ZSMJ7%% as follows: b1=a1%%ZSMJ8%%, ∀i>1,bi=bi−1⊕ai%%ZSMJ9%%, where ⊕%%ZSMJ10%% is the bitwise exclusive-or (xor). After constructing an array b%%ZSMJ11%%, the constraint b1<b2<⋯<bn−1<bn%%ZSMJ12%% should hold.
Since the number of possible arrays may be too large, you need to find the answer modulo m%%ZSMJ13%%.
input: The first line contains an integer t%%ZSMJ14%% (1≤t≤100%%ZSMJ15%%) denoting the number of test cases in the input.
Each of the next t%%ZSMJ16%% lines contains two integers d,m%%ZSMJ17%% (1≤d,m≤109%%ZSMJ18%%).
Note that m%%ZSMJ19%% is not necessary the prime!
output: For each test case, print the number of arrays a%%ZSMJ20%%, satisfying all given constrains, modulo m%%ZSMJ21%%.
